title: Engineering: measurement and modelling
covers: Field monitoring of equipment and buildings, building-energy and techno-economic models, system models and scenarios.

adapted_from.name: Sovacool, Axsen & Sorrell 2018, code of practice for quantitative energy modelling
ASHRAE Guideline 14 calibration thresholds (NMBE ≤5%, CV(RMSE) ≤15% monthly; 10% and 30% hourly), as quoted by OSTI
Fowlie, Greenstone & Wolfram 2018 (modelled savings about 2.5× realised)
Gleeson & Lowe 2013 (heat pump SPF boundaries, 622 systems)
UK Electrification of Heat project (open monitoring data, cleaning rules)

questions.text: Do the main figures rest on field measurement, or on a model calibrated or validated against measurement with its error stated? Manufacturer ratings or an unvalidated model are 'not found'.
Is the system boundary stated: what the measurement or model includes and excludes (for a heat pump, which seasonal-performance boundary)?
Are the number of sites or systems and the period covered stated, and adequate (for heating, at least one full heating season)?
Is uncertainty reported: measurement accuracy, data-cleaning or completeness rules, or the model's error or sensitivity ranges?
Are the key assumptions (prices, weather, occupancy, efficiencies, costs) stated, with their sources?
Do claims about savings, costs or performance stay within the conditions that were measured or modelled?
Are the results compared with other measured studies, a baseline, or another model?
Are data, code or model inputs published, and are funding and conflicts of interest stated?
